title: Where it grows
subtitle: Campania and Basilicata
objectives: Explain the role of volcanic soils

steps.title: Two regions
steps.body: Aglianico grows mainly in Campania, around Naples and inland in Irpinia, and in Basilicata, on the slopes of Monte Vulture. Smaller amounts grow in Puglia and Molise. There are some plantings in Australia and California, but it remains overwhelmingly Italian.

steps.title: Volcanoes and height
steps.body: Both key areas are volcanic: Irpinia has volcanic ash over clay and limestone; Vulture is an extinct volcano. Volcanic soils drain well and give a smoky, mineral edge. Altitude, often 400 to 700 m, gives cool nights. Together they explain how a late grape ripens slowly and keeps freshness.

steps.prompt: Monte Vulture, in Basilicata, is an extinct volcano.
steps.explanation: Yes. Its volcanic slopes give Aglianico del Vulture its character.

steps.body: Look for Aglianico from Campania labelled Irpinia or Taburno. They're often cheaper than Taurasi and show the grape's character well.

steps.prompt: What do volcanic soils give Aglianico?
options: Good drainage and a smoky edge
steps.explanation: Volcanic soils drain well and are often linked to smoky, mineral notes.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Aglianico grows mainly in Campania and Basilicata
Volcanic soils drain well and add a smoky edge
Altitude gives cool nights for slow ripening
